cues.cap: This is Coach Connect, the new way clients register with the Kentucky SBDC and book their first coaching appointment, all in one visit.
Let’s walk through it as a client, and see what happens behind the scenes.
There are four steps: your details, your business, review and consent, and your appointment.
Our sample client is Maya Brooks, who runs a catering business in Louisville. Step one is her contact information.
Clients who aren’t in business yet just use their home address.
Not ready for one-on-one coaching? The banner up top points to the no-cost training calendar.
The ZIP code does the routing. The moment it’s typed, the form shows the center that serves her: Louisville.
ZIPs outside our map go to the Eastern Kentucky intake team, so nobody hits a dead end.
When she clicks Continue, her contact details are saved right away, even if she never finishes.
Step two asks where she is in her business journey: starting a business, or already in business.
Already in business adds a few fields, and the form requires at least one full-time or part-time employee.
Then, in her own words, how we can help.
Demographic questions come last. Each offers Prefer not to say, except Sex, which is Male or Female. None of it affects the coaching match.
Step three puts every answer on one screen, with a link back to edit.
Two boxes are required: the client agreement, and a certification that she’s eligible for taxpayer-funded services.
Her signature has to match the name she entered. The SBA mailing permission is optional.
Register and choose appointment records her registration in Neoserra.
Now she picks a coach from the center that serves her. Louisville shows each coach’s photo and specialties.
Maya’s planning a storefront, so Claire Bridges, who lists restaurant and catering operations, is a natural fit.
Her choice is saved, and Claire’s Calendly opens right in the page, with Maya’s name and email filled in.
She picks a time, and she’s on the calendar. Calendly emails the confirmation, and the booking is noted on her client record.
Lexington adds a first-available option, and other centers show a simple list.
If the record note can’t be saved, the booking still stands, and the client gets a retry button.
So behind the scenes, there are five handoffs.
The ZIP picks the center. Continue saves the contact. Register records the client. The coach’s calendar opens. And the booking lands on the record.
Registering a client yourself? Start a new registration clears the form for the next person.
Clients who get stuck can call 1-888-414-7232, weekdays from 8 to 5.
Coach Connect. Register, match, and book, all in one visit.
Send clients to register.kentuckysbdc.com.
